content.comment_body: Hello, what is the best method to show, on the front panel of [product_name], how long a machine has been running today? I also want it to restart tracking the next day to monitor machine downtime. Thank you.

70% OFF-TOPIC Hi, Reading your post, my first thought was: "Here is someone hoping for a ready-made solution." But seeing [user_name] as your name, I know that's not the case. I propose you create a sample program and let us know where you encounter issues. This way, you learn the most. We can then help you move forward—does that sound okay? If you're under time pressure, feel free to disagree or skip my suggestion. [user_name], what do you think?

You can set up a counter yourself. Use an asynchronous pulse generator to create pulses every second. Count the seconds while the motor is ON, and use another counter for the OFF state. By dividing total seconds by 3600, you get the hours. You can reset at any time—this is a flexible way to obtain an hour counter.

Hello, Thank you for responding. My other posts are for personal learning, as I purchased [product_name] hardware to improve my skills with [company_name]'s products. I appreciate everyone’s assistance. Back to the topic: I’ll put together a sample and share it here.
Please check if I'm heading in the right direction. I just need guidance on how to obtain the final result.
Are there any files available to review, besides empty folders?

Hello [user_name], There is a specific function for your requirement: Hour Counter. With it, you can set: - OT: Operating time—duration machine runs. - MI: Maintenance interval—the next maintenance time. - MN: Time until next maintenance. MN = OT - MI (hh:mm) These times can be displayed and reset partially or completely. If you want maintenance scheduling by weekdays, change input I1 to connect a Weekly Timer enabling the Hour Counter function. See attached draft for reference.
Hi, thanks for the example. I tested it in the simulation and now understand how the output works. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: User aims to show daily machine runtime and downtime on a hardware interface using [company_name] automation products. There are initial questions about the most effective method. Community responses explain both the built-in hour counter function and custom approaches using timers and counters. Through trial and discussion, the user learns to use the built-in solution. Overall, the learning process highlights the need for clearer documentation and user-friendly tutorials for those self-teaching this subject.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects a straightforward and dependable way to display and reset daily machine operation hours directly on the device, preferably utilizing built-in functions whenever available.
